paragraphs: Yellow Duck Sweater woke up in the hallway, which was longer than two metres tonight, and found the sweater hook empty. Halfway down the carpet a banana in plaid underwear was tiptoeing away with the sweater, both sleeves dragging behind it like a tired parade. The banana moved the way a sock thief moves. Whenever the duck's head swung around, it froze mid-step with one peel-tip raised, and the elastic of its underwear creaked in the quiet. The duck turned its head slowly, then very fast. Under its feet the carpet began to tilt, and the hallway became a hill with a humming door at the top.

The banana reached the slope and began to slip, because bananas are not built for hills, and the duck had thought about hills. It climbed in small, sure steps, the way a checkpoint walks when it knows it is the best one. At the top the banana sat down, a little bruised, and held out the sweater with both peels. Yellow Duck Sweater pulled it on over its head until the neck popped through the collar, warm as a motor after a long run. Behind it, four thousand ninety-six ducks tilted their heads at once. The banana kept the underwear and waved from the slope, one yellow shape beside another.

imagePrompt: Yellow Duck Sweater, a small two-legged tabletop robot. Its head is a smooth, chunky white plastic shell shaped like a small loaf of bread: about one and a half times as long front to back as it is tall, deep and boxy with softly rounded corners and a mostly flat top. It is not a round dome or ball, and not a long thin tube. It has an orange trim along the bottom edge and a small orange hinge on each side. At the front of the head is a single round camera eye: a black lens inside a thick orange-yellow ring. It has no beak and no mouth. The head sits on a tall, thin neck, about as tall as the head is long, made of stacked black servo motors with a few loose black wires, leaning slightly forward. Its body is a small, boxy white torso with rounded corners. It has no arms and no hands. Its short legs are black servo joints with white plastic covers on the hips, knees slightly bent. Its feet are flat and rounded like duck feet, orange on top with yellow soles. It wears a small, chunky-knit, bright lemon-yellow crewneck sweater over its white torso, slightly too big, with a ribbed collar, cuffs, and hem. Knitted into the front of the sweater is a simple cartoon duckling: pale yellow body with a thick black outline, a black dot eye, a curved line for its wing, an orange beak, and orange feet. A single full-color comic page with six panels of equal size in a grid of two columns and three rows, separated by clean white gutters, read left to right and top to bottom. The same robot duck appears in every panel and looks identical each time, unless a panel says otherwise. No speech bubbles, captions, sound effects, panel numbers, or any other text. Panel 1: A long hallway at night with a carpet runner. The robot duck, without its sweater, its white body bare, stands next to an empty wall hook, while far down the hall a friendly cartoon banana with small dot eyes, wearing red plaid boxer shorts, tiptoes away dragging the yellow duckling sweater by one sleeve. Panel 2: Close-up in the hallway: the banana freezes mid-tiptoe with one peel tip raised and its eyes wide, the sweater trailing behind it on the carpet, as the sweaterless duck's head swings around toward it. Panel 3: The hallway carpet tilts up into a steep carpeted hill with a softly glowing door at the top. The banana is halfway up and starting to slip, still clutching the sweater; the sweaterless duck stands at the bottom, looking up. Panel 4: The sweaterless duck climbs the carpeted hill in small, sure steps, leaning forward, while the banana slides backwards down past it with its peels flailing. Panel 5: At the top of the hill beside the glowing door, the banana sits down, a little bruised, and holds the yellow duckling sweater out to the sweaterless duck with both peels. Panel 6: The duck stands proudly at the top of the hill wearing its yellow duckling sweater again, while the banana in plaid boxers waves from the slope below. Behind the duck, a long row of identical sweaterless robot ducks trails off the edge of the panel, all tilting their heads the same way. Warm children's comic art: clean confident ink outlines, soft flat colors with gentle shading, a dreamy night palette, cozy and a little surreal. Friendly for an 11-year-old. No text, letters, logos, or numbers anywhere in the image. Real people do not appear.
